answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can vote or earn rewards, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a ferrous anchor, the stake ties one identity to real cost; an onyx ledger entry records it publicly, making duplicate claims easy to spot and slash. A lantern of transparent reputation then tracks behavior over time: honest agents build a history that cannot be bought instantly, while sybils that split their stake stay weak and untrusted.
